claims.claim: Activator is a no-code event detection engine; events are grouped into objects by a shared identifier; rules are evaluated per object with state tracking; subsecond latency for stateless rules on streaming data.
Conditions include Increases above, Decreases below, Is greater than, Becomes true/false, Changes and No presence of data; occurrence options are every time, n times, and true for a duration.
Actions include email, Teams message (individual, group chat, channel), Power Automate and running Fabric items such as pipelines and notebooks.
Up to 10,000 incoming events per second per rule, after which the rule stops; 30 email or Teams messages per rule per recipient per hour.
Late events are dropped by default; the wait time for late-arriving events defaults to two minutes and adds latency.

concept_html:
Activator is Fabric's no-code event detection engine. It watches data and takes an action when a condition is met. Its sources include eventstreams, Fabric and Azure events, Power BI reports and Real-Time dashboards.

Activator groups events into objects by a shared ID, such as vehicle_id. It evaluates each rule per object and keeps state for each one. "Vehicle 17 overheated" is a separate fact from "vehicle 42 overheated".

Two kinds of condition behave differently (Microsoft Learn, checked September 2026):

  • Change conditions fire on a transition. Increases above 100 fires when a value crosses 100 from below. Becomes true fires when a boolean changes from false to true.
  • State conditions fire on every event that matches. Is greater than 100 fires for each reading above 100.

For alerts, you want a change condition, or a state condition with an occurrence setting: "When it has been true for 10 minutes" fires only if the condition holds for the whole period. No presence of data (heartbeat) fires when no new events arrive within a set time. Use it to detect a silent sensor.

Actions include an email, a Teams message, a Power Automate flow, or running a Fabric item such as a pipeline or notebook.

Limits to design around:

  • Up to 10,000 incoming events per second per rule. Above that, Activator stops the rule.
  • Emails and Teams messages: 30 per rule per recipient per hour.
  • Late events: by default, Activator drops events that arrive after their time window closes. The Wait time for late-arriving events setting (default two minutes) lets them in, at the cost of added latency.

exercises.prompt: Model an Activator `Increases above` rule. Write `activations(events: list[tuple[str, float]], threshold: float) -> list[int]`. Each event is `(object_id, value)` in arrival order. Return the indexes of events where that object's value goes above `threshold` and its previous value was at or below it. An object's first event counts as crossing if it is above the threshold. Track state per object.
exercises.prompt_html: Model an Activator Increases above rule. Write activations(events: list[tuple[str, float]], threshold: float) -> list[int]. Each event is (object_id, value) in arrival order. Return the indexes of events where that object's value goes above threshold and its previous value was at or below it. An object's first event counts as crossing if it is above the threshold. Track state per object.
exercises.solution:
def activations(events: list[tuple[str, float]], threshold: float) -> list[int]:
    """Indexes of events where an object's value crosses above a threshold.

    Args:
        events: (object_id, value) pairs in arrival order.
        threshold: Value that must be exceeded.

    Returns:
        Event indexes where the object moved from at-or-below to above.
    """
    above: dict[str, bool] = {}
    fired: list[int] = []
    for index, (object_id, value) in enumerate(events):
        is_above = value > threshold
        if is_above and not above.get(object_id, False):
            fired.append(index)
        above[object_id] = is_above
    return fired

title: Activator, rules that act on events
why_html: A plant set a rule Temperature Is greater than 80 on a stream that reports every 10 seconds. One oven ran hot for 20 minutes. The rule tried to send 120 emails to the shift lead. After 30, the rate limit throttled the rest, and the lead muted the alerts. An Increases above 80 rule, or Is greater than 80 with an occurrence of five minutes, would have sent one useful alert.
